attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Show that projected auxiliary variables cannot evade unconditional DNNF lower bounds.
attacks.method: Existentially forget all auxiliary variables from the claimed polynomial d-DNNF by replacing their literals with true. This preserves decomposability and does not increase size, yielding an ordinary DNNF for the original CNF. Apply an explicit CNF family with exponential DNNF lower bounds.
attacks.notes: The contradiction is independent of the local grammar, scheduler, certificates, and runtime. H016 universally promises a polynomial DNNF for families known to require exponential DNNF size.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use known exponential savings from auxiliary variables to rescue H016.
attacks.method: Distinguish a smaller d-DNNF before forgetting from the ordinary DNNF obtained after forgetting. The auxiliary-variable construction can remove determinism and save size relative to d-DNNF, but it still outputs a DNNF after projection and therefore cannot beat lower bounds against all DNNFs.
attacks.notes: The previously recorded auxiliary-variable defence A036 attacked only deterministic lower bounds and did not survive the stronger ordinary-DNNF closure argument.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Find an algorithm satisfying the written bounds without deciding SAT.
attacks.method: Choose an algorithm that retains only the root residual, creates no accepting path, and halts. The class bound and accepting-path witness condition hold vacuously, but satisfiable formulas are not accepted.
attacks.notes: The statement omits coverage and two-sided correctness, so its claimed consequence does not follow. H018 is terminally rejected as malformed rather than disproved after repair.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Verify that the certificate restriction also restricts all computation performed by Q.
attacks.method: Observe that H018 restricts residual merges but does not forbid arbitrary computation before exploration or require exploration to be the decision mechanism.
attacks.notes: Even after adding completeness, a repaired descendant must bound the entire algorithm rather than only merge certificates.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Test whether a fixed finite local grammar genuinely excludes a hidden general computation.
attacks.method: Finite bounded-radius rewrite systems can simulate polynomial-time machines through local state transitions. Constant local truth-table checks alone therefore do not establish that the compiler is structurally weaker than an arbitrary polynomial-time algorithm.
attacks.notes: No contradiction was derived, but H009 still needs a preserved invariant or a non-universality theorem before it counts as an independent mechanism rather than a syntactic implementation language.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Apply known lower bounds for polynomial calculus with extension variables over finite fields.
attacks.method: Compare the model in H010 with lower bounds where each extension variable depends on at most O(log n) original variables, and with stronger extension-rule lower bounds over the rationals.
attacks.notes: H010 permits recursively composed fan-in-two extensions with global support and works over GF(2); the known theorems do not literally cover this exact system. They sharply narrow the next attack target.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Show that parity extraction plus generic local Tseitin rewrites remains capable of simulating arbitrary polynomial computation.
attacks.method: Audit the generic bounded-radius rewrite component separately from Gaussian elimination. Fan-in-two Boolean definitions and local transitions are computationally universal unless an invariant limits their global composition.
attacks.notes: The parity component is not the only source of power. H017 needs a formal invariant preserved by every allowed non-affine rewrite before separator lower bounds can target it cleanly.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Hide global semantic power inside an undefined Boolean interface node treated as one boundary symbol.
attacks.method: Inspect whether the interface DAG language, node semantics, allowed gate set, and certificate expansion cost are fully bounded rather than counting an arbitrarily complex subfunction as one symbol.
attacks.notes: The total node bound helps, but the exact interface language and certificate composition rules remain underspecified. A lower-bound target cannot be fixed until these are formalized.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Find an unconditional theorem settling weak automatability of TC0-Frege.
attacks.method: Compare the exact statement with fixed-depth NP-hardness results and classical or quantum cryptographic conditional hardness.
attacks.notes: The strongest located results remain conditional for TC0-Frege or unconditional for fixed-depth Frege. They do not settle H015.

attacks.targeted_failure_mode: Use the 2026 hard-CNF result to refute polynomial boundedness of unrestricted full IPS.
attacks.method: Check whether the theorem proves lower bounds for arbitrary algebraic circuits or only roABP-IPS and related restricted fragments.
attacks.notes: The result reaches Boolean CNFs but remains restricted to roABP-based IPS. H014 survives as a full-circuit proof-size frontier.
